description_summary: 12-month unduplicated student headcounts, broken down by undergraduate/graduate level, sex, and race/ethnicity. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYLEV. The table includes old and new race/ethnicity fields, plus derived combined categories from the 2009-10 transition to the new reporting categories.

12-month instructional activity for undergraduate and graduate education, reported as total credit hours and/or contact hours delivered. Query this table for instructional volume used to derive 12-month full-time-equivalent enrollment, rather than for unduplicated student headcounts.

Academic library data for 2009-10 include library characteristics, collections, expenditures, and services, with a subset of variables retained for consistency with the 2014-15 IPEDS collection. The table is institution-level, applies only to degree-granting institutions, and includes expenditure data only for institutions with total expenditures over $100,000; no separate even- or odd-year reporting restriction is stated.

Awards conferred from July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2010, reported by 6-digit Classification of Instructional Programs (CIP) code, first or second major, award level, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by IPEDS institution ID (UNITID), CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL; the table includes certificates and degrees, total awards, awards for men and women, and race/ethnicity-specific award counts. Because 2009-10 was the final year of the three-year race/ethnicity reporting transition, the table contains old and new race/ethnicity variables plus derived combined categories, including Two or more races.
Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, attendance status, and student level (EFLEVEL).

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, attendance status, and student level (EFALEVEL), with counts for all nine race/ethnicity categories.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, age category (EFBAGE), and student level (LSTUDY). Age enrollment reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2010 (even) is an optional year and age data may be absent for institutions that did not report it.

First-time freshman counts broken down by state of residence, including the number who graduated from high school the previous year. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and state of residence (EFCSTATE). Residence reporting is optional in odd-numbered years; 2010 (even) is not an optional year under that rule.

Fall enrollment counts for selected major fields, broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. It covers four-year institutions only and includes Education, Engineering, Biological/Life Sciences, Mathematics, Physical Sciences, Business Management and Administrative Services, Law, Dentistry, and Medicine; each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, major field, attendance status, and student level (EFCIPLEV).

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio, with one record per institution identified by UNITID. The table applies only to institutions with undergraduate students; only academic-year institutions report entering-class data, and institutions offering programs shorter than one year do not have retention data.

Institution-level finance records identified by UNITID for public institutions using GASB 34/35 accounting standards, including revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities.

Institution-level finance records identified by UNITID for all private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB accounting standards, including revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities.

Institution-level finance records identified by UNITID for private for-profit institutions using FASB accounting standards, including revenues by source, expenditures by category, and assets and liabilities.

Graduation-rate outcomes at 200% of normal time for bachelor’s-seeking cohorts at 4-year institutions and degree/certificate-seeking cohorts at less-than-4-year institutions; the cohorts entered in 2002 and 2006, respectively, and include completion within 100%, 150%, or 200% of normal time. The 200% measure is reported only in odd-numbered years, so 2010 (even) has no data for this table.

Graduation-rate outcomes at 150% of normal time for 4-year and 2-year institution cohorts, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity. Records are uniquely defined by UNITID and GRTYPE: 4-year cohorts entered in 2004 and include bachelor’s and other degree/certificate seekers, while 2-year cohorts entered in 2007; the table includes old, new, and derived race/ethnicity categories, but 100%-of-normal-time completions are not available by gender and race/ethnicity for 2-year institutions.

Graduation-rate outcomes at 150% of normal time for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates at less-than-2-year institutions, using the 2007 entering cohort. Institution-level counts cover the cohort enrolled and those completing within 100% or 150% of normal time or transferring out.

Staff counts broken down by occupational category, tenure or faculty status, medical-school status, and full- versus part-time status. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPRECTP, which encodes the occupational category, tenure status, and work status.

Fall staff counts broken down by occupational category, race/ethnicity, gender, and full- versus part-time status. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SABDTYPE; race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2010 (even) may have no data.

Employee counts at degree-granting institutions with fewer than 15 full-time employees, all nondegree-granting institutions, and related administrative offices, broken down by primary function or occupation, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SCNLEVEL; race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2010 (even) may have no data.

Full-time instruction, research, and public-service staff counts at degree-granting institutions with at least 15 full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by faculty or tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK, which combines faculty status and academic rank; race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2010 (even) may have no data.

Full-time new-hire counts at degree-granting institutions with at least 15 full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by primary occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and SGTYPE; race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2010 (even) may have no data.
Counts and salary outlays for full-time, nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by gender, academic rank, and contract length. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, ARANK, and CONTRACT.

Counts of full-time nonmedical instructional staff with contracts shorter than 9 months, broken down by gender and academic rank. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and ARANK; the less-than-9-month contract restriction is fixed for this table.

Fringe-benefit recipients, total expenditures, and average expenditures for full-time nonmedical instructional staff, broken down by contract length and benefit-plan type. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and BENTYPE.

Counts of full-time nonmedical instructional staff in 4-year institutions, broken down by faculty status, contract length, gender, and academic rank. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CONTRACT, and ARANK.

An indicator showing which institutions submitted a custom comparison group for the 2011 Data Feedback Report. The row grain is one institution identified by UNITID; this indicator first became available for 2010-11 and therefore is available for 2010 (even).

Membership in institution-submitted custom comparison groups for the 2011 Data Feedback Report, listing the submitting institution and each comparison institution’s UNITID, name, and state. The row grain is a submitting-institution/comparison-institution pair, identified by the submitting institution UNITID and comparison institution UNITID.

Survey-component response and applicability statuses for each institution, including nonresponse with imputed data, parent/child or multi-campus reporting, and revised-submission indicators. The row grain is institution by survey component, identified by UNITID and the component identifier.

Institution directory and classification information, including names and locations, contact and web links, active status, Title IV participation, control, level, highest award, and Carnegie classifications. The row grain is one institution identified by UNITID.

Institutional offerings, award levels, control and affiliations, special learning opportunities, admissions policy, applicants, admissions, and admissions-test information. The row grain is one institution identified by UNITID; applicant, admission, and test-score fields apply only to institutions that do not have open admissions.

Student charges for full academic-year programs, including undergraduate and graduate tuition and fees, part-time per-credit charges, professional-practice charges, and published first-time undergraduate cost-of-attendance amounts. The row grain is one institution identified by UNITID, and this table applies to institutions with primarily credit-hour academic programs using a semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or other academic-year calendar.

Student charges by program for vocational or occupational offerings, including the number of programs, charges and cost of attendance for the largest program, and tuition, fees, and books and supplies for up to five additional programs. The row grain is one institution identified by UNITID; it applies to institutions using clock-hour programs or primarily occupational credit-hour programs and reports charges for the full program length.
An institution’s mission statement or the web address where it is posted. The row grain is one institution identified by UNITID.

Institution-level counts of undergraduate aid recipients and total and average aid amounts, broken down by aid source and type. The rows distinguish full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates—reported for federal, state/local, institutional, and federal or nonfederal loan aid—from all undergraduates, for whom total grants, Pell grants, and federal loans are reported.

Institution-level average net price and its underlying financial-aid amounts for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in two distinct groups: those receiving grant or scholarship aid and those receiving Title IV federal aid. For public institutions, both groups are restricted to students paying in-district or in-state tuition; the table includes values for 2007-08, 2008-09, and 2009-10.
